card.statement:
For $x\in H^{*}_{T}(X;k)$, the operator $\Sigma_{x}^{T}$ satisfies the following properties.

(i)

$\Sigma_{1}^{T}=\mathrm{id}$ for $1\in H^{0}_{T}(X;k)$, the unit class.

(ii)

$\Sigma_{cx}^{T}=c^{p}\Sigma^{T}_{x}$ for $c\in\Lambda^{\prime}=k[z^{\alpha}:\alpha\in H_{2}^{\mathrm{eff}}(X;\mathbb{Z})]$ a constant.

(iii)

$\Sigma_{x}^{T}(x_{0})|_{(t,\theta)=0}=\overbrace{x\star_{T}\cdots\star_{T}x}^{p}\ast_{T}\ x_{0}$.

(iv)

$\Sigma_{x}^{T}(x_{0})|_{z^{\alpha}=0}=\mathrm{St}^{T}(x)\smile_{T}x_{0}$, where $\mathrm{St}^{T}(b)\in H^{*}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(X;k){[\![t,\theta]\!]}$ is the total Steenrod power in $T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}$ -equivariant cohomology, and $\smile_{T}$ is the $(T\times\mathbb{G}_{m})$ -equivariant cup product.

(v)

$\Sigma_{x\star_{T}x^{\prime}}^{T}=(-1)^{\frac{p(p-1)}{2}|x||x^{\prime}|}\Sigma_{x}^{T}\circ\Sigma_{x^{\prime}}^{T}$.

Property (ii) is just Frobenius-linearity. Property (iii) claims that quantum Steenrod operators are equivariant deformations of the $p$ -th power operation in quantum cohomology, and (iv) claims that the quantum Steenrod operators are quantum deformations of the Steenrod operations in mod $p$ cohomology. Property (v) is called the quantum Cartan relation, which shows that quantum Steenrod operators $\Sigma_{x}^{T}$ collectively define an algebra action from the (Frobenius-twisted) mod $p$ ( $T$ -equivariant) quantum cohomology algebra. In particular, the actions of $\Sigma_{x}^{T}$ and $\Sigma_{x^{\prime}}^{T}$ graded commute for any $x,x^{\prime}$ by the graded commutativity of $\star_{T}$.

The main result of [Lee23] is the identification of quantum Steenrod operators on degree $2$ classes for conical Hamiltonian symplectic resolutions with the $p$ -curvature of the quantum connection. Recall from Section 2.3.3 that the quantum connection is a $k[\![t,\theta]\!]\otimes H^{*}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m}}(\mathrm{pt})$ -linear operator

(3.14)

$\nabla_{x}:=t\partial_{\bar{x}}+x\ \star_{T}:H^{*}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m},loc}(X;\hat{\Lambda})[\![{t,\theta}]\!]\to H^{*}_{T\times\mathbb{G}_{m},loc}(X;\hat{\Lambda})[\![{t,\theta}]\!]$

where $\partial_{\bar{x}}$ acts on $z^{\alpha}\in\hat{\Lambda}$ by $\partial_{\bar{x}}z^{\alpha}=\langle\alpha,\bar{x}\rangle z^{\alpha}$. Here, $t$ is the equivariant parameter for the $\mu_{p}(\mathbb{C})$ -action on the source curve for holomorphic maps $u:\mathbb{P}^{1}\to X$ counted for defining the quantum connection, which we later identify with the equivariant parameter for the $\mathbb{G}_{m}(\mathbb{C})$ -action on the target $X$ (see 2.28).
card.label: Proposition 3.7

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
